audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer phases[N].side reads 'Skill' while content win[N] reads Neeko on all seven rows. The page renders a flat coinflip chart above prose that says you win every stage of the lane.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Neeko on all seven rows, identical to the content layer, and the win rate is 53.77% over 212 games. Every content why argues a Neeko advantage grounded in the range and mobility gap: he has no dash, your E is 1000 range, and his stun is delivered by a basic attack.
audit.corrected: phases[0..6].side -> Neeko across the board. All seven existing whys already argue Neeko, so no why needed rewriting to match.

audit.why: Level 3 completes root-into-bloom on an immobile target, level 6 gives you an all-in he cannot answer up close while his own 6 is map pressure rather than duelling, and both item spikes keep you the aggressor. spikes[0..3] carry this, and spikes[1] correctly says his level-6 spike is roams, not a lane duel.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important mechanic is nowhere on the page: Pick a Card's gold stun is delivered by a BASIC ATTACK, not by the cast, and the W is an auto-attack reset. The page tells the reader to 'back off the moment it glows yellow', which is the wrong cue — the card can glow for a long time while he walks. The cue is the step-and-swing. Also unstated: Pick a Card is 6s flat at every rank, Wild Cards travels 10000 units on a 5-6s cooldown, Stacked Deck adds damage every fourth attack, and Destiny reveals every enemy champion at 5500 range on 170s at rank 1.
audit.why: enemyKit W flags carry autoReset and hardCC with text 'uses that for his next attack'; E text 'Every 4 attacks, Twisted Fate deals bonus damage'; R text 'revealing all enemy champions and enabling the use of Gate'. missingInteractions rule 'autoreset-burst-tell' names exactly this gap: the wind-up is the cue to step back, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[0].d now all key off the attack that delivers the stun rather than the card lighting up.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contains no digit at all, and two of its three bullets are generic Neeko lines that would fit any enemy in the lane.
audit.why: Defect-catalogue item 3. Kit supplies W 6s flat, Q 6/5.75/5.5/5.25/5, R 170/140/110.
audit.corrected: Rebuilt around the flat 6s W, the 5-6s Q, and the 170s Destiny as the roam clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated mechanics in the content layer. whys[0] and early both credit Neeko with sustain from her passive — 'P minion heals', 'P heal on minions'. Neeko's passive is a disguise; there is no heal anywhere in her kit. spikes[0].text says the E-Q layers 'on a slowed target' (Neeko has no slow) and that TF's 'only escape is Blue Card's mana or flashing' — Blue Card restores mana, it is not an escape.
audit.why: ownerKit P text is entirely about looking like an ally champion and what breaks the disguise; no heal flag on any Neeko ability. No slow flag on any Neeko ability either. enemyKit has no dash on any ability, so Flash genuinely is his only exit — that half is right, the Blue Card half is not.
audit.corrected: whys[0] and early now win the early game on faster clear and his 60 mana per Wild Cards; spikes[0] now says rooted, not slowed, and names Flash as his only exit.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects reports '1 probable wrong ability name' pointing at 'Gold Card' in spikes[1].text and suggesting 'Wild Cards'. This is a FALSE POSITIVE — Gold Card is the correct name for the stun variant of Pick a Card and is used correctly there. Separately, dosFull[1].d is the tradeGood string, dontsFull[1].d is the generic clone paragraph under a root title, and dontsFull[2].d is the tradeBad string — three bled bullets.
audit.why: packet.suspectNames matched at distance 3 on a legitimate card name; defect-catalogue item 2 covers the bleed.
audit.corrected: No name change made. All three bled bodies replaced with content matching their own titles.

notes: CHART: content win[0..6] already matches packet.levelChart (Neeko on all seven rows), so only the flat full-layer sides were moved; no no-op win[N] edits proposed. No side flip changed a verdict direction — every row moved from 'Skill' to 'Neeko', which all seven existing whys already argue — so no why needed rewriting to stay consistent. Ratings untouched. FALSE POSITIVE CONFIRMED: packet.suspectNames flags 'Gold Card' in spikes[1].text as probably 'Wild Cards'; Gold Card is the correct name of the stun variant and no edit was made. TWO FABRICATIONS CORRECTED IN CONTENT: Neeko was credited with passive minion healing in both whys[0] and early — her passive is a disguise and she has no heal in the kit at all — and spikes[0] called the E-Q target 'slowed' (Neeko has no slow) while naming 'Blue Card's mana' as an escape (it restores mana; Flash is genuinely his only exit, which is why the rest of that entry stands). whys[0] and early keep their Neeko verdict, so correcting them does not disturb the chart. The biggest remaining gap the fix closes is the stun's delivery: the page told the reader to react to the card glowing, when the card can stay lit indefinitely — the actual tell is the auto-attack wind-up, exactly as missingInteractions says.
